title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”
slides: OpenAI just cut its models off from the live internet. Why now?
The change follows warnings about unverified data reaching training pipelines.
Rivals like Anthropic still scrape live web content, betting on fresh data.
Enterprises relying on real-time knowledge may see slower model updates.
Ask your vendor: is your model still learning from the open web?
thread_text:
1. OpenAI's Quiet Cutoff

OpenAI has severed its models from the live internet, and the timing is no accident. The company cites a flood of unverified data reaching its training pipelines.

2. The Warning That Triggered It

Insiders had flagged that scraped web content was slipping past verification filters. OpenAI chose to freeze real-time access rather than risk poisoning its models.

3. Rivals Are Doubling Down

Anthropic and others are still scraping live web content, betting that fresh data beats clean data. That's a direct philosophical split on how AI should learn.

4. Enterprises Feel It First

Companies relying on real-time knowledge will see slower model updates. Their AI may lag behind breaking events while rivals keep pulling from the open web.

5. Ask Your Vendor Today

Is your model still learning from the open web? Check your contract and ask for data provenance. If they can't answer, you have your answer.
